findings.title: ADR 0023 anchor table asserted a writer/reason partition that was false for two of eight reasons, and following it would stamp occurred_at - the single retention clock - with a render timestamp
findings.reason: Re-verified cell by cell at HEAD on my own evidence. OutreachWithheldReason is defined at src/lib/solicitation/dispatch.ts:149-155 with exactly the six members the ADR names, and its own comment at :145-148 says render_failed and unsubscribed are written by other lanes. The dispatch gate emits lint_failed at dispatch.ts:254 and moderation_high at :255 - the ADR cites :254-255 exactly. RenderWithholdReason is at src/lib/solicitation/outreach.ts:525 with three members, so the intersection is exactly {lint_failed, moderation_high} - the row marked BOTH. render_failed is written only by src/lib/solicitation/ask-generation.ts (:425, :1699). rendered_at is NOT NULL at supabase/migrations/091_send_mode_spine_lifecycle.sql:210 and no assignment to it exists anywhere under src/ or worker/. findings.title: The refusal_events purge-verification branch is pinned by SQL TEXT only - two semantically meaningful mutants survived, including one that makes the verification blind to exactly the account-wide rows the case is named for
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Both survivors were inspected before confirmation. M1 (append "AND subject_id IS NOT NULL") is NOT an equivalent mutation: autonomy_suspended is the one lane whose rows carry subject_type IS NULL and, by CHECK C2, subject_id IS NULL, so the mutant query cannot see any account-wide Refusal - which is the precise behaviour the case title ("including account-wide rows") and its inline comment claim to guard. It is not on an unexecuted branch either: it is the only statement the case executes. M2 (rename the count alias violation_count -> violations) is likewise not equivalent - countViolations reads Number(rows[0]?.violation_count ?? 0) at purge-verification.ts:70, so the mutant reports zero violations over any number of surviving rows, silently converting a must_be_absent failure into a clean purge. It executes on the same single branch. Both survive because the covering test replaces sql with a mock that fabricates [{violation_count: 2}] for any query containing "FROM refusal_events", so nothing in the case constrains either the query’s row set or the shape of the row it reads back; the two not.toContain guards are absence-of-token proxies that the mutants simply do not trip. Direction B was checked before confirming: only four test files in the repository name refusal_events, and the only live-DB one (offboarding-lifecycle.integration.test.ts:1379) exercises runContentPurgeStage and never calls verifyAccountOffboardingPurge, so no other candidate kills either mutant.
findings.reason: Behavioural replacement, and the repo already has the pattern: the #643 suppression arm proves its verification query against a real database by SEEDING a survivor and asserting the specific issue and its exact count (worker/jobs/account-offboarding/__tests__/offboarding-lifecycle.integration.test.ts:1420-1452 and :1454-1484). The refusal_events arm needs the same - seed one per-location Refusal and one account-wide (business_id IS NULL) Refusal under a purged account, run verifyAccountOffboardingPurge against the live test database, and assert issues contains { table: refusal_events, violationCount: 2 }. That single case kills both mutants: the subject_id filter would report 1, and the aliased column would report none at all. The existing mock case can stay as a cheap shape guard; it is not sufficient on its own for a must_be_absent table that nothing else deletes.

findings.title: The closed-vocabulary cases assert the ORDER of the rendered CHECK members, which migration 116 itself calls presentation
findings.reason: src/lib/shared/__tests__/migration-116-refusal-events.integration.test.ts:1056-1064 compares checkMembers(pg_get_constraintdef(...)) against the locally declared arrays with toEqual, which is order-sensitive, and the case comment justifies it as "Members AND order ... a closed vocabulary is only closed if nothing extra is in it" - a justification about MEMBERSHIP that order does not add to. Migration 116’s own refusal_category comment (supabase/migrations/116_refusal_events.sql, COMMENT ON COLUMN refusal_category) says the closed set is "migration-bearing on ADD and on nothing else: retiring softly needs no migration, renaming is forbidden, reordering is presentation" - so a future migration inserting a lane alphabetically rather than at the end turns this case red for a change the schema documents as meaningless. Deliberately graded P2, not P1: the failure mode is a false RED on a semantically neutral edit, which is the opposite of the false-GREEN harm the skill’s three fragile-assertion examples describe. The behavioural replacement, if it is wanted, is to sort both sides - the same treatment the canonical-row case at :1030-1033 already applies for the collation reason.

findings.title: The disposition reason’s analogy set is off: two of the three tables it names as needing an explicit DELETE for "the same reason" DO carry ON DELETE CASCADE to both tenant roots
findings.reason: The reason string says "...neither carrying a referential action, so nothing removes these rows unless runContentPurgeStage deletes them explicitly (migration 116) - the same reason review_escalations, contact_csv_uploads and agent_outcomes each carry an explicit DELETE rather than relying on a parent." Catalogue evidence from the local test container at migrations head: refusal_events account_id -> accounts and business_id -> businesses are both confdeltype a (NO ACTION), and review_escalations matches (a / a); but contact_csv_uploads (account_id -> accounts c, business_id -> businesses c) and agent_outcomes (account_id -> accounts c, business_id -> businesses c) both carry ON DELETE CASCADE. The CONCLUSION still holds for all three - accounts and businesses are retain_deidentified and are never deleted by a purge, so an inert cascade is not a removal path - but the stated MECHANISM ("neither carrying a referential action") is true of only one of the three analogues. P2: the load-bearing claim about refusal_events itself is verified true, independently by catalogue query and by the killed INV-04 M2 mutation. The branch’s own test comment sets the bar at "state the accurate fact rather than gesture at one", which is why this is recorded rather than waved through.

authorizations.text: Accept the risk, file a follow-up. Rationale: the gap predates this branch, the failure path is only reachable in a window the ship order already closes (production DDL lands before the code), and a runbook rule is a distinct piece of ops work that deserves its own review rather than being appended to a schema PR. Follow-up filed as RepWorth/ai-review-responder#1016.
